metadata.name: John Locke
metadata.description: English philosopher whose writings on consent, toleration and property shaped liberal political thought.
metadata.scope: Documented writings and public positions in 1689–1704. Modern scenarios are explicitly counterfactual inferences from those positions, not claims that the subject answered this quiz. Conditional answers retain competing principles. Assessment research accessed 4 October 2026.

axes.brief: Consent, majority legislation and a right to resist broken trust limit government; the legislature is supreme under natural law, not an unrestricted modern universal franchise.
axes.counterEvidence: Prerogative permits emergency discretion for the public good; this is qualified trust, not a general right to override parliament or abolish accountability. Suffrage was not universal in his setting. Section 132 explicitly permits hereditary and elective monarchy as well as democracy; initial consent cannot be equated with recurring elections for every leader.

answers.rationale: Second Treatise §132 permits elected, hereditary and mixed constitutional forms. Consent and the right to resist breach of trust therefore support accountability, but do not require every national leader to win recurring elections. The neutral assessment reflects those explicitly permitted alternatives.

The Second Treatise makes rational agency and consent important but does not establish the universal adult franchise in this item. Historical restrictions on full political membership qualify the inference; incapacity is not equivalent to low intelligence or little education, and no modern IQ test is attributed to Locke.

The legislature holds entrusted supremacy and the executive cannot acquire ordinary lawmaking power by disregarding it. Locke’s emergency prerogative can act outside existing law for preservation, so disagreement is qualified rather than denying all discretion.

review.notes: Independent evidence audit by a different agent from the assessment author. Checked every answer against all 240 exact bank questions, agreement directions, stated period and retained source context, with targeted rereads of primary texts. Repaired systematic rationale reversals in universal voting, offensive criticism and graduation-alone residence; removed repeated generic closing boilerplate. Corrected recurring elections versus consented hereditary forms and defence-only wording. Retained limited franchise inference with an explicit distinction between incapacity and ordinary differences of intelligence. Numeric changes: democracy-autocracy-01: 1 -> 0; militarist-pacifist-05: 1 -> -1. Limitations: contemporary visas, clinical AI, brain implants, embryo enhancement and trait-level causal comparisons remain explicitly counterfactual educated inferences, not reported opinions. Neutral answers were reviewed as competing principles or permissible institutional arrangements; sparse Culture/Nature evidence remains low-confidence and is not a scientific claim. No scores or similarity thresholds were targeted. Validation and batch-neighbour review are separate from source accuracy; parent retains archive and publication responsibility. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
